acceptance: A sweep running write_primitives then transaction_primitives, and tpcds then tpcds_obt, on the same platform succeeds.
The guard still refuses to drop a database holding tables BenchBox did not create.
context: Evidence: release-v2 run 40971306663 (tag v0.5.0rc2, commit b1459438d), artifacts release-uat-v0.5.0rc2-stage3-olap and release-uat-v0.5.0rc2-stage3-postgres-family: cells.jsonl, uat_gate_summary.json, validator_rollup.tsv, uat_lifecycle.log and per-cell logs.
description: benchbox/platforms/base/connection_lifecycle.py:253 refuses to drop a database that holds tables not owned by the current benchmark. Benchmarks that share a database name now fail in sequence: transaction_primitives after write_primitives on Doris, SingleStore and pg_duckdb (batch_metadata, bulk_load_ops_target, insert_ops_* ...), and tpcds_obt after tpcds on SingleStore and pg_mooncake. Decide whether these benchmarks should use distinct database names, whether the guard should treat tables of known BenchBox benchmarks differently, or whether UAT should pass --force-recreate, without weakening protection for user tables.
